html:
SMTO-SKL-0141 — Slack files can only be moved inside a conversation

GUID: 7ece2528-54b7-56b6-9830-f2692bd21a1d
Slug: slack-artifact-context-required
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • SMTO keeps files you send to or get from Slack inside a conversation. This request didn't come with one, so SMTO didn't send or download anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open a Conversation with the Agent (or start a new one) and ask it there to upload or download the Slack file. Files moved to or from Slack must belong to a conversation, and this request had none.
  2. For uploads, make sure the file was created or attached in that same conversation before asking to send it. SMTO only sends files that belong to the conversation asking for them.
  3. If you started this from somewhere other than a conversation, try the same request from a conversation instead. Only requests made during a conversation carry the place where Slack files are stored.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reports the file was uploaded to the channel, or the downloaded file appears in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting where you started the request from. Nothing was sent to Slack, so there is nothing to undo.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack file transfer was refused because the tool context has no artifact store or no run_id/conversation_id artifact scope.

What this means

  • Slack file transfer has no artifact registry or run/conversation ownership context. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack file transfer has no artifact registry or run/conversation ownership context.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the execution's artifact context and active scope.

How to fix it

  • files.artifact_context requires _artifact_store plus _artifact_scope.run_id and conversation_id in the execution context. Invoke slack.upload_file or slack.download_file through a normal Agent run in a conversation, and check that the calling path passes the run's artifact registry and scope.
  • Run the transfer in a conversation with an active run artifact workspace.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The transfer runs in the intended active artifact workspace.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
